messages:
maya: seeing a sharp latency/throughput regression on qwen2.5 hosted pods since the 2026-03-16 deploy. p95 up ~45%, throughput down ~18%. profiler shows a lot of generic matmul fallback instead of the fwd_attn kernel. also noticed KV cache invalidations on long CJK prefixes. attaching profiler snippet and tokenizer diff.

alex: can you paste the profiler trace and an example input that reproduces? p95 numbers + pod id would help.

maya: repro input (shortened): 
`你好，世界` repeated 20x -> previously ~800 tokens, now ~1024. profiler excerpt: 
```
# profiler top frames
0x7f3a kernel_selector.cpp:142 select_kernel_autokernel_v2()
0x7f3a matmul_generic.cu:88 generic_matmul()
0x7f3a fwd_attn_opt.cu: -- not hit --
0x7f3a kv_cache.cpp:211 invalidate_prefix_if_misaligned()
Trace: kernel=generic_matmul ratio=0.64, attn_opt=0.12, kv_cache_miss=0.22
```

samir: repro pod: redispatch-3c4f. ran a local micro-bench with cpu profiler + nvtx, confirmed kernel selector choosing generic path when seq_len distribution has many odd-length CJK tokens. command I used: 
`./infra/tools/run_perf --model qwen2.5 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --trace nvtx`

julia: two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenization boundaries for CJK are changing the offset -> KV cache alignment breaks so we fall back; 2) model metadata's kv/attn projection dims mismatched so kernel_selector thinks layout incompatible and forces generic matmul. Qwen variants historically have 2 ways of packing heads -> attn_heads vs kv_heads. check model metadata: 
```
model.json excerpt:
"attn_heads": 32,
"kv_heads": 16,  # unexpected
"head_dim": 64
```
If kv_heads != attn_heads or kv_proj_dim != head_dim*kv_heads we hit code path that triggers layout-normalization and kernel fallback.

maya: I dug into tokenizer diffs: the new tokenizer merge table regressed for zh -> produces more surrogate tokens and changes join offsets. example tokenization diff: 
```
old: ["你", "好", "，", "世界"] -> offsets [0,3,6,9]
new: ["你好", "，", "世界"] -> offsets [0,6,9]
```
The mismatched offsets shift KV cache indexing for cached prefixes.

perf-bot: alert: gpu_p95_latency increased 48% on qwen2.5 pool (pods affected: redispatch-3c4f, redispatch-7b2d). gpu_util unchanged. memory_bw +4%.

samir: quick mitigation: add runtime flag `--kv_cache_strict_alignment=true` to treat shifted offsets as aligned (forces index remap) OR force kernel selector to prefer attn_opt: `KERNEL_SELECTOR=attn_opt_v3` (temporary). I tested override on a single pod, p95 dropped to +8% (better).

alex: thanks. can you open a minimal reproducer and a bisect? sounds like two separate bugs: tokenization/merge-table change, and model metadata mismatch. I can run a kernel-selector bisect across releases if you link the commit range.

julia: note: changing `kv_cache_strict_alignment` is a bandaid. correct fix is: 1) ensure tokenizer deterministic segmentation for zh in our tokenizer config for qwen2.5; 2) update model loader to validate kv_heads vs attn_heads and reject/repair inconsistent model.json; 3) add a unit test to the kernel selector for head dim compatibility. Also check ALiBi vs RoPE flag: if model claims RoPE but we load ALiBi variant we get different rotary dims which affect kernel packing.

maya: plan: opening issue and linking repro + profiler + pod logs. temp mitigation: roll `KERNEL_SELECTOR=attn_opt_v3` on 30% of pool, enable `kv_cache_strict_alignment=true` on that canary. julia will submit model-loader validation PR. assigning: maya -> open issue + canary roll, julia -> PR for loader validation, samir -> run bisect kernel selector and send results. Alex will coordinate release rollback if canary fails.

alex: +1. please add timeline and rollback hook. ping me when the issue is created. :thumbsup:
